cards.title: Look forward to + -ing
cards.summary: Significa «tener muchas ganas de» algo. Aquí to es una preposición, así que después va un sustantivo o un verbo con -ing.
uses: Expresar ilusión por algo futuro: I'm looking forward to the trip.
Cerrar correos formales: I look forward to hearing from you.
Con un verbo, siempre en -ing: looking forward to seeing you.

pitfalls.wrong: I look forward to see you.
pitfalls.right: I look forward to seeing you.
pitfalls.why: Aquí to es preposición, no parte del infinitivo: después va -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I'm looking forward for the weekend.
pitfalls.right: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
pitfalls.why: La preposición es siempre to, nunca for.

pitfalls.wrong: I look forward to hear from you.
pitfalls.right: I look forward to hearing from you.
pitfalls.why: En los correos formales es hearing, con -ing.

examples.en: I'm looking forward to the weekend.
examples.es: Tengo muchas ganas de que llegue el fin de semana.

examples.en: We're looking forward to seeing you.
examples.es: Tenemos muchas ganas de verte.

examples.en: The kids are looking forward to going to the beach.
examples.es: Los niños tienen muchas ganas de ir a la playa.

cards.title: Presente perfecto o pasado simple
cards.summary: El pasado simple habla de algo terminado, normalmente con un momento concreto (yesterday, in 2019). El presente perfecto une el pasado con el presente: experiencias y cosas sin fecha.
cards.form: have/has + participio (sin fecha) · verbo en pasado + momento concreto
uses: Experiencias sin fecha: Have you ever been to Peru?
Algo reciente que importa ahora: I have lost my keys.
Con yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago y en preguntas con when: pasado simple (When did you arrive?).
En inglés americano también es muy común el pasado simple para algo reciente, incluso con just, already y yet: I just ate. Did you finish yet? I lost my keys.

pitfalls.wrong: I have seen that movie yesterday.
pitfalls.right: I saw that movie yesterday.
pitfalls.why: Con un momento concreto (yesterday) se usa el pasado simple.

pitfalls.wrong: When have you arrived?
pitfalls.right: When did you arrive?
pitfalls.why: Las preguntas con when piden un momento concreto: pasado simple.

pitfalls.wrong: I have visited Rome two years ago.
pitfalls.right: I visited Rome two years ago.
pitfalls.why: Con ago siempre va el pasado simple.

examples.en: I have been to Peru twice.
examples.es: He estado en Perú dos veces.

examples.en: I went to Peru in 2019.
examples.es: Fui a Perú en 2019.

examples.en: Have you ever tried sushi?
examples.es: ¿Alguna vez has probado el sushi?

examples.en: She has lost her keys, so she can't get in.
examples.es: Perdió las llaves, así que no puede entrar.

examples.en: When did you arrive?
examples.es: ¿Cuándo llegaste?

examples.en: We saw that movie last week.
examples.es: Vimos esa película la semana pasada.

cards.title: Primer condicional
cards.summary: Habla de una situación real o probable en el futuro y de su resultado: if + presente, will + verbo.
cards.form: if + presente simple, will + verbo base
uses: Consecuencias probables de algo que puede pasar.
Advertencias y promesas: If you touch it, you will get hurt.
La parte con if puede ir al principio (con coma) o al final (sin coma).

pitfalls.wrong: If it will rain tomorrow, we will stay home.
pitfalls.right: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home.
pitfalls.why: Después de if va el presente, aunque hable del futuro (como en español: si llueve).

pitfalls.wrong: If I see him, I tell him.
pitfalls.right: If I see him, I will tell him.
pitfalls.why: Para el resultado en el futuro se usa will: I will tell him (se lo diré).

pitfalls.wrong: If you don't hurry, you will to miss the bus.
pitfalls.right: If you don't hurry, you will miss the bus.
pitfalls.why: Después de will va el verbo sin to.

examples.en: If it rains, we will stay home.
examples.es: Si llueve, nos quedaremos en casa.

examples.en: If you study, you will pass the test.
examples.es: Si estudias, aprobarás el examen.

cards.title: Segundo condicional
cards.summary: Habla de situaciones imaginarias o poco probables en el presente o el futuro: if + pasado, would + verbo.
cards.form: if + pasado simple, would + verbo base
uses: Situaciones imaginarias: If I had more time, I would travel.
Dar consejos: If I were you, I would call her.
Con be, were sirve para todas las personas (if I were…); was también es común.

pitfalls.wrong: If I would have money, I would buy a car.
pitfalls.right: If I had money, I would buy a car.
pitfalls.why: Después de if no va would: se usa el pasado (had).

pitfalls.wrong: If I am you, I would call her.
pitfalls.right: If I were you, I would call her.
pitfalls.why: Para imaginar, después de if va el pasado: were (o was).

pitfalls.wrong: If I won the lottery, I will travel.
pitfalls.right: If I won the lottery, I would travel.
pitfalls.why: Con if + pasado, el resultado lleva would, no will.

examples.es: Si tuviera más tiempo, aprendería a tocar la guitarra.

cards.title: Verbo + -ing o verbo + to
cards.summary: Algunos verbos van seguidos de -ing (enjoy, finish) y otros de to + verbo (want, decide). Con stop y remember, el significado cambia.
cards.form: enjoy / finish + -ing · want / decide + to + verbo · stop y remember: los dos, con otro significado
uses: Enjoy, finish, mind + -ing: I enjoy cooking.
Want, need, decide, hope + to: I want to rest.
Stop + -ing = dejar de; stop + to = detenerse para.
Remember + -ing = recordar algo pasado; remember + to = acordarse de hacer algo.

pitfalls.wrong: I enjoy to cook.
pitfalls.right: I enjoy cooking.
pitfalls.why: Enjoy siempre va con -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I want going home.
pitfalls.right: I want to go home.
pitfalls.why: Want va con to + verbo.

pitfalls.wrong: He stopped to smoke last year.
pitfalls.right: He stopped smoking last year.
pitfalls.why: Dejar de hacer algo es stop + -ing; stop to smoke significa detenerse para fumar.

pitfalls.wrong: Remember locking the door when you leave.
pitfalls.right: Remember to lock the door when you leave.
pitfalls.why: Para acordarse de hacer algo después se usa remember + to.

cards.title: Make, let y have + persona + verbo
cards.summary: Las tres van con una persona y un verbo sin to. Make es obligar, let es dejar o permitir, y have es encargarle a alguien que haga algo.
cards.form: make / let / have + persona + verbo base (sin to)
uses: Make: obligar o provocar (My boss made me work late. The movie made me cry.).
Let: permitir (My parents let me go to the party.).
Have: encargar un trabajo a alguien (I had the mechanic check the brakes.).

pitfalls.wrong: My mom made me to clean my room.
pitfalls.right: My mom made me clean my room.
pitfalls.why: Después de make + persona, el verbo va sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: They don't let us to use our phones.
pitfalls.right: They don't let us use our phones.
pitfalls.why: Let + persona + verbo, sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: My parents allowed me go out.
pitfalls.right: My parents let me go out.
pitfalls.why: Allow sí lleva to (allow me to go out); let no.

pitfalls.wrong: I had the mechanic to check the brakes.
pitfalls.right: I had the mechanic check the brakes.
pitfalls.why: Con have + persona, el verbo también va sin to.

examples.en: My boss made me work late.
examples.es: Mi jefe me hizo trabajar hasta tarde.

examples.en: That movie made me cry.
examples.es: Esa película me hizo llorar.

examples.en: My parents let me go to the party.

cards.title: El futuro: will, be going to y presente continuo
cards.summary: Will sirve para decisiones del momento, promesas y predicciones; be going to, para planes e intenciones; el presente continuo, para planes ya acordados.
cards.form: will + verbo · am / is / are going to + verbo · am / is / are + verbo-ing (+ cuándo)
uses: Will: decisiones del momento, ofrecimientos y promesas (I'll help you).
Will: predicciones y opiniones (I think the rent will go up).
Be going to: planes e intenciones ya decididos (We're going to move next year).
Presente continuo: citas y planes acordados con fecha (I'm meeting Ana on Friday).

pitfalls.wrong: I will to call you tomorrow.
pitfalls.right: I will call you tomorrow.
pitfalls.why: Después de will va el verbo sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: The phone is ringing. I answer it.
pitfalls.right: The phone is ringing. I'll answer it.
pitfalls.why: Para una decisión del momento («yo contesto») se usa will, no el presente.

pitfalls.wrong: Tonight I go to the movies with Ana.
pitfalls.right: Tonight I'm going to the movies with Ana.
pitfalls.why: Para un plan ya acordado se usa el presente continuo, no el presente simple.

pitfalls.wrong: I think it's raining tomorrow.
pitfalls.right: I think it will rain tomorrow.
pitfalls.why: Para una opinión sobre el futuro se usa will o going to.

examples.es: El lunes almuerzo con Ana.

examples.es: No te preocupes, te ayudo con las cajas.

examples.en: I think the rent will go up again.
examples.es: Creo que el alquiler va a volver a subir.

examples.en: What are you doing this weekend?
examples.es: ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?

examples.en: She's going to look for a bigger apartment.
examples.es: Va a buscar un apartamento más grande.

cards.title: Oraciones de relativo: who, which, that, where
cards.summary: Unen dos ideas y dicen de quién o de qué hablas: who para personas, which para cosas, that para las dos y where para lugares.
cards.form: persona + who / that · cosa + which / that · lugar + where
uses: Who para personas: The woman who sings in the band is my neighbor.
Which para cosas: The laptop which I bought is very fast.
That puede reemplazar a who o which, sobre todo al hablar: the phone that I bought.
Where para lugares: the theater where we saw the play.

pitfalls.wrong: The actor which won the prize is Mexican.
pitfalls.right: The actor who won the prize is Mexican.
pitfalls.why: Para personas se usa who (o that), no which.

pitfalls.wrong: This is the app what I use.
pitfalls.right: This is the app that I use.
pitfalls.why: El «que» relativo es that o which, nunca what.

pitfalls.wrong: That's the restaurant where we had dinner there.
pitfalls.right: That's the restaurant where we had dinner.
pitfalls.why: Where ya indica el lugar: no se repite there.

pitfalls.wrong: The phone that I bought it doesn't work.
pitfalls.right: The phone that I bought doesn't work.
pitfalls.why: That ya reemplaza al objeto: no se repite it.

examples.en: The woman who sings in the band is my neighbor.
examples.es: La mujer que canta en la banda es mi vecina.

examples.en: This is the theater where we saw the play.
examples.es: Este es el teatro donde vimos la obra.

examples.en: I need a charger that works with this phone.
examples.es: Necesito un cargador que funcione con este teléfono.

examples.en: The laptop which I bought last week is very fast.
examples.es: La laptop que compré la semana pasada es muy rápida.

examples.en: He's the director who made that movie.
examples.es: Es el director que hizo esa película.

examples.en: Is there an app that can translate this?
examples.es: ¿Hay alguna aplicación que pueda traducir esto?

cards.title: La voz pasiva: presente y pasado
cards.summary: Pone el foco en lo que pasa o pasó, no en quién lo hace: is / are o was / were + participio. Suele traducirse con «se» (se habla, se construyó).
cards.form: am / is / are + participio · was / were + participio · (+ by + quién lo hace)
uses: Cuando no importa o no se sabe quién hace la acción: My bike was stolen.
Procesos y productos: These phones are made in Korea.
Noticias e historia: The news was announced on TV.
By indica quién lo hizo: The article was written by a young journalist.

pitfalls.wrong: The app was create in 2015.
pitfalls.right: The app was created in 2015.
pitfalls.why: La pasiva lleva el participio (created), no el verbo base.

pitfalls.wrong: English speaks in many countries.
pitfalls.right: English is spoken in many countries.
pitfalls.why: «Se habla» se dice con la pasiva: is spoken.

pitfalls.wrong: The phones was made in Korea.
pitfalls.right: The phones were made in Korea.
pitfalls.why: Con un sujeto plural se usa were (o are).

pitfalls.wrong: The news was announced from the president.
pitfalls.right: The news was announced by the president.
pitfalls.why: Quién hace la acción se introduce con by, no con from.

examples.en: English is spoken in many countries.
examples.es: El inglés se habla en muchos países.

examples.en: These phones are made in Korea.
examples.es: Estos teléfonos se fabrican en Corea.

examples.en: My password was changed yesterday.
examples.es: Ayer se cambió mi contraseña.

examples.en: The website was updated last week.
examples.es: El sitio web se actualizó la semana pasada.

examples.en: The news was announced on TV.
examples.es: La noticia se anunció en la televisión.

examples.en: The article was written by a young journalist.
examples.es: El artículo lo escribió un periodista joven.

cards.title: Estilo indirecto: said, told y asked
cards.summary: Sirve para contar lo que otra persona dijo o preguntó. El verbo suele ir un tiempo más atrás: «I'm tired» → She said she was tired.
cards.form: said (that) + oración · told + persona + (that) · told + persona + to + verbo · asked + if / wh- + sujeto + verbo
uses: Contar lo que alguien dijo: He said (that) the test was easy.
Tell lleva a quién: She told me (that) she was busy. Para órdenes: The teacher told us to be quiet.
Los tiempos retroceden: am → was, will → would, can → could.
Preguntas indirectas: She asked if I was ready. He asked me where I lived (sin did y sin invertir el sujeto).

pitfalls.wrong: He said me that he was tired.
pitfalls.right: He told me that he was tired.
pitfalls.why: Say no lleva a la persona directamente: said that o told me that.

pitfalls.wrong: She asked me where did I live.
pitfalls.right: She asked me where I lived.
pitfalls.why: En la pregunta indirecta no se usa did y el sujeto va antes del verbo.

pitfalls.wrong: The teacher told us finish the essay.
pitfalls.right: The teacher told us to finish the essay.
pitfalls.why: Para contar una orden se usa told + persona + to + verbo.

pitfalls.wrong: He asked me that I was ready.
pitfalls.right: He asked me if I was ready.
pitfalls.why: Una pregunta de sí o no se cuenta con asked if (o whether).

examples.en: She said she was tired.
examples.es: Dijo que estaba cansada.

examples.en: The teacher told us the exam would be easy.
examples.es: La profesora nos dijo que el examen sería fácil.

examples.en: He told me to hand in my homework on Friday.
examples.es: Me dijo que entregara la tarea el viernes.

examples.en: My friend asked if I could help her.
examples.es: Mi amiga me preguntó si podía ayudarla.

examples.en: She asked me where I lived.
examples.es: Me preguntó dónde vivía.

examples.en: They said they had finished the project.
examples.es: Dijeron que habían terminado el proyecto.

cards.title: Used to: hábitos del pasado
cards.summary: Used to + verbo habla de hábitos o situaciones del pasado que ya no ocurren. Equivale a «solía» o al pretérito imperfecto (antes comía…).
cards.form: used to + verbo base · didn't use to + verbo base · did you use to…?
uses: Hábitos del pasado: I used to smoke, but I gave up.
Situaciones que cambiaron: She used to live in Lima.
Negativas y preguntas sin -d: I didn't use to exercise. Did you use to play sports?
Para hábitos del presente se usa usually, no used to: I usually walk to work.

pitfalls.wrong: I use to eat a lot of sugar when I was young.
pitfalls.right: I used to eat a lot of sugar when I was young.
pitfalls.why: En afirmativas es used to, con -d.

pitfalls.wrong: I didn't used to exercise.
pitfalls.right: I didn't use to exercise.
pitfalls.why: Después de didn't va use, sin -d.

pitfalls.wrong: I used to go to the gym now.
pitfalls.right: I usually go to the gym now.
pitfalls.why: Used to es solo pasado; para el presente se usa usually.

pitfalls.wrong: He used to working at night.
pitfalls.right: He used to work at night.
pitfalls.why: Después de used to va el verbo base, no -ing.

examples.en: I used to eat a lot of fast food.
examples.es: Antes comía mucha comida rápida.

examples.en: She used to smoke, but she gave up last year.
examples.es: Ella fumaba, pero lo dejó el año pasado.

examples.en: We didn't use to exercise much.
examples.es: Antes no hacíamos mucho ejercicio.

examples.en: Did you use to play any sports at school?
examples.es: ¿Hacías algún deporte en la escuela?

examples.en: My grandfather used to walk every day.
examples.es: Mi abuelo caminaba todos los días.

examples.en: I used to sleep only five hours a night.
examples.es: Antes dormía solo cinco horas por noche.

cards.title: Pasado continuo
cards.summary: Was / were + verbo-ing describe una acción que estaba en curso en un momento del pasado. Suele combinarse con el pasado simple: «estaba estudiando cuando llamaste».
cards.form: was / were + verbo-ing · pasado continuo + when + pasado simple · while + pasado continuo
uses: Una acción en curso en un momento del pasado: At eight, I was studying.
Una acción larga interrumpida por otra corta: I was taking notes when the teacher called me.
Dos acciones al mismo tiempo, con while: While I was reading, she was cooking.
Describir la escena de una historia: It was raining and everyone was waiting.

pitfalls.wrong: I was study when you called.
pitfalls.right: I was studying when you called.
pitfalls.why: Después de was o were va el verbo con -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: We was taking an exam.
pitfalls.right: We were taking an exam.
pitfalls.why: Con we, you y they se usa were.

pitfalls.wrong: I studied when you called me.
pitfalls.right: I was studying when you called me.
pitfalls.why: La acción que estaba en curso va en pasado continuo; la que la interrumpe, en pasado simple.

pitfalls.wrong: I was knowing the answer.
pitfalls.right: I knew the answer.
pitfalls.why: Verbos como know, want o like casi nunca van en forma continua.

examples.en: I was studying when you called.
examples.es: Estaba estudiando cuando llamaste.

examples.en: What were you doing at nine last night?
examples.es: ¿Qué estabas haciendo anoche a las nueve?

examples.en: She was taking notes while the teacher was talking.
examples.es: Ella tomaba apuntes mientras el profesor hablaba.

examples.en: It was raining when we left school.
examples.es: Estaba lloviendo cuando salimos de la escuela.

examples.en: They weren't listening to the teacher.
examples.es: No estaban escuchando al profesor.

examples.en: I fell asleep while I was reading.
examples.es: Me quedé dormido mientras leía.

cards.title: Deducciones: must, can't y might
cards.summary: Sirven para sacar conclusiones sobre algo que no sabes con seguridad: must (seguro que sí), can't (seguro que no) y might (quizás).
cards.form: must / can't / might + verbo base · might not + verbo base
uses: Must: estás casi seguro de que es verdad (She must be tired = debe de estar cansada).
Can't: estás casi seguro de que no es verdad (That can't be Ana. She's in Spain.).
Might (o may, could): es posible, pero no seguro (The tickets might be sold out).
Van con el verbo base, muchas veces be: must be, might be, can't be.

pitfalls.wrong: He mustn't be at home. The lights are off.
pitfalls.right: He can't be at home. The lights are off.
pitfalls.why: Para «seguro que no» se usa can't; mustn't expresa una prohibición.

pitfalls.wrong: She must to be the director.
pitfalls.right: She must be the director.
pitfalls.why: Después de must va el verbo sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: It might is expensive.
pitfalls.right: It might be expensive.
pitfalls.why: Después de might va el verbo base (be), no is.

examples.en: The theater is full. The play must be very good.
examples.es: El teatro está lleno. La obra debe de ser muy buena.

examples.en: That can't be the singer. She's too young.
examples.es: Esa no puede ser la cantante. Es demasiado joven.

examples.en: The tickets might be sold out.
examples.es: Puede que las entradas estén agotadas.

examples.en: You must be tired after the concert.
examples.es: Debes de estar cansado después del concierto.

examples.en: He might not like the movie.
examples.es: Quizás no le guste la película.

examples.en: It can't be true!
examples.es: ¡No puede ser verdad!

cards.title: Unless: a menos que
cards.summary: Unless significa «a menos que» o «si no». Como if, va seguido del presente aunque hable del futuro.
cards.form: unless + presente, will + verbo · unless = if… not
uses: Una condición negativa: We will lose the forests unless we act now.
Equivale a if… not: unless you hurry = if you don't hurry.
Después de unless va el presente, aunque se hable del futuro.
El verbo después de unless va en afirmativo: unless it rains (no unless it doesn't rain).

pitfalls.wrong: Unless we will recycle, there will be more waste.
pitfalls.right: Unless we recycle, there will be more waste.
pitfalls.why: Después de unless va el presente, como después de if.

pitfalls.wrong: I won't go unless you don't come.
pitfalls.right: I won't go unless you come.
pitfalls.why: Unless ya es negativo: el verbo que sigue va en afirmativo.

pitfalls.wrong: We can't save energy unless turn off the lights.
pitfalls.right: We can't save energy unless we turn off the lights.
pitfalls.why: Después de unless hace falta un sujeto: unless we turn off…

examples.en: Unless we act now, the climate will keep changing.
examples.es: Si no actuamos ahora, el clima va a seguir cambiando.

examples.en: Don't throw it away unless it's broken.
examples.es: No lo tires a menos que esté roto.

examples.en: Unless you turn off the lights, you'll waste energy.
examples.es: Si no apagas las luces, vas a desperdiciar energía.

examples.en: I won't buy a car unless I really need one.
examples.es: No voy a comprar un auto a menos que de verdad lo necesite.

examples.en: We'll go by bike unless it rains.
examples.es: Iremos en bicicleta a menos que llueva.

cards.title: Have to, must, don't have to y mustn't
cards.summary: Have to y must expresan obligación. En negativa cambian mucho: don't have to es «no hace falta» y mustn't es «está prohibido».
cards.form: have to / must + verbo base · don't have to (no es necesario) · mustn't (está prohibido) · had to (pasado)
uses: Have to: obligaciones que vienen de afuera, como reglas o el trabajo (I have to wear a uniform).
Must: algo que quien habla considera necesario, o reglas escritas (You must arrive on time).
Don't have to: no es obligatorio, puedes elegir (You don't have to come).
Mustn't: no está permitido (You mustn't use your phone in the exam). En pasado se usa had to.

pitfalls.wrong: You mustn't come to the meeting if you are busy.
pitfalls.right: You don't have to come to the meeting if you are busy.
pitfalls.why: Si algo no es necesario se usa don't have to; mustn't significa que está prohibido.

pitfalls.wrong: I must to finish this report today.
pitfalls.right: I must finish this report today.
pitfalls.why: Después de must va el verbo sin to.

pitfalls.wrong: Yesterday I must work late.
pitfalls.right: Yesterday I had to work late.
pitfalls.why: Must no tiene pasado: se usa had to.

pitfalls.wrong: She don't have to work on Fridays.
pitfalls.right: She doesn't have to work on Fridays.
pitfalls.why: Con he, she o it: doesn't have to.

examples.en: I have to finish this report by Friday.
examples.es: Tengo que terminar este informe para el viernes.

examples.en: You must arrive on time for the interview.
examples.es: Debes llegar a tiempo a la entrevista.

examples.en: You don't have to wear a suit on Fridays.
examples.es: No hace falta que uses traje los viernes.

examples.en: You mustn't share your password with anyone.
examples.es: No debes compartir tu contraseña con nadie.

examples.en: I had to work late yesterday.
examples.es: Ayer tuve que trabajar hasta tarde.

examples.en: Does she have to travel for work?
examples.es: ¿Ella tiene que viajar por trabajo?
